$comment: The wac compiler this repo is verified against. A minimum — a newer checkout is fine
and is the normal state — but one that is *kept current* rather than left at the oldest
commit that happens to still work.
Update it proactively, whenever the suite has just passed and wac has moved (operator,
2026-08-05). The old rule here was 'bump it only when you adopt a compiler feature that
did not exist before', and the failure of that rule is measurable: this pin sat at a
2026-08-03 commit while wac went 52 commits ahead, and nobody knew whether the claim was
still true. It was — every package still built against it when somebody finally checked —
but an untested claim is not evidence, and the note the harness prints had become noise
Only ever move it to a commit the suite has actually passed against; `deno task wac:pin`
records the sibling checkout's HEAD. The reason field is for whoever reads a failure six
weeks from now: name the feature when a feature is why, and say 'routine' when it is not.
See 'Keeping the compiler pin current' in README.md. Checked by
harness/wacVersion.ts on the first wacBind of a run.
reason: routine: the suite passed against this compiler in the gate run that pushed it — the pin tracks a recently verified compiler, not the oldest conceivable one
